svg.text: How Vinboo works
The slideshow lives on the presenter's device — and in hand-off mode it goes on living on the screens.
WHILE THE PRESENTER IS THERE
Presenter's browser
phone · laptop · tablet
Photos and .pptx files
read straight off the device
• Renders PowerPoint into SVG slides
• Holds the playlist and running order
• Answers requests for single slides
Two ways to share, chosen here
Live — this tab is the only copy, so it
must stay open. Hand-off — every screen
takes a copy, and then it need not.
Everything here happens in the browser:
files are read locally, and a .pptx is
unzipped and drawn with no round trip.
Vinboo server
Node · HTTP/1.1 behind Railway's TLS edge
• Accounts, sign-in, sessions
• Issues share codes and passwords
• Parks each viewer's request for a slide
• Hands it to whoever can answer
No media on disk, ever
A slide sits in memory only while in
flight, plus the last six frames of a
show. No volume is attached.
Ten screens on one slide cost a single
upload: the reply is fanned out to
everyone waiting on it.
Viewers
as many as you like · no account
Television
Laptop
Phone
Every screen keeps a copy
In hand-off mode each screen quietly
stores the whole show as it plays.
Any browser will do, and nothing is
installed. Cast sends a television to
/watch, which it then loads itself.

AFTER THE PRESENTER LEAVES — HAND-OFF MODE
The tab that started the show can close, provided one screen still holding a full copy is open. That screen becomes the source.
Presenter's tab — closed
the laptop is shut, or gone home
Nothing of the show is left behind on
it that anybody still needs. The photos
were never uploaded, and the copies
that matter are already on the screens.
If no copy is online
a late screen is told so plainly, rather
than left waiting for a photo.
Vinboo server — unchanged
the same relay, pointed at a new source
• Parks the same requests as before
• Hands each job to a screen instead
• Still stores no pictures of its own
The presenter keeps first refusal
A screen is only given work when no
presenter poll is parked, so while that
tab is open the originals stay the source.
A screen with the whole show
any one will do · no account, still no app
SOURCE
others watch,
and hold copies
of their own
Only a complete copy may serve
A screen that holds every slide can answer for the
rest; a half-copied screen is never asked.
offers to serve

answers
PUT …/frame/:id
a late screen
GET …/photo/:i
150 slides · 1 to 48 hours, extendable once
Transport
Every hop between a browser and Vinboo is HTTPS. Railway's edge
terminates TLS and forwards to the app over HTTP/1.1.
Slides travel as raw binary bodies carrying their own type — no
base64, no re-encoding, no transcoding.
Waiting is long-polling: a GET is held open for up to 25 seconds
— 30 for a slide — and answered the instant something changes.
The seeding path in purple above uses exactly the same two calls.
What it deliberately is not
No WebSockets, no WebRTC. Every exchange above is an ordinary
HTTP request and response, which is why it survives corporate
proxies and hotel Wi-Fi without special handling.
Not peer-to-peer. Even when one screen feeds another, it goes
through the relay. No screen ever learns another's address.
Not end-to-end encrypted. TLS protects each hop separately, so the server can read a slide in passing.
